evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: H1 'Know what your city council is about to decide, before the meeting.' plus lede 'Commonread reads it, writes each item in plain language, and emails you when your street or a topic you follow is on it' and a neighbourhood+email form directly below. As a resident I could repeat what it does and what to do after one screen.
evidence.fit: Every audience gets its own path: nav links 'En español' and 'For clerks and funders'; a full Spanish section ('Si hablas español en casa') with a ✓/✕ list saying summaries are English-only; a clerks/funders table ('Partner cities: None yet', 'Funding: None yet'); a neutrality box 'What a summary never does'. The model-draft + volunteer-check process and the 'Open the original agenda item' link are present. Against that, the no-backend constraint is handled by a mailto to alerts@commonread.org, an address the brief never supplied, and the page invents a named pilot city (Linden Falls) as fact.
evidence.distinctiveness: The packet-vs-summary pair (all-caps ordinance text 'REZONE ASSESSOR PARCELS 031-22-004 THROUGH 031-22-011' beside a four-part plain summary) and the yellow highlighter motif on 'Oakdale Avenue' come from the product. The rest is a familiar structure: three numbered steps, tinted alternating sections, a three-column footer.
evidence.proof: 1440: the alert card is in the first viewport and changes when you pick a neighbourhood (I picked Mill District: subject became 'Mill District is on next Tuesday's council agenda' and the original-item link changed to #item-6a; Eastgate gave an honest 'Nothing about Eastgate' empty state). The second screen shows the original text next to the summary, and a five-item agenda with a 'Draft, not yet checked by a volunteer' item. Strong material, but none of it is labelled as an example; it is presented as a real city's real agenda.
evidence.craft: 1440: clean serif type, a calm navy/yellow palette and a consistent rhythm. The right column of the hero ends at y≈570 and leaves a blank area under the card. probe: one axe colour-contrast violation at 390 and 1440. The agenda excerpt in the .doc block is set at 0.86rem monospace, which is dense to read.

The alert card, the page's artifact, starts at y≈961, below the 844 fold, so choosing a neighbourhood swaps a card you can't see. After a valid submit the 'Almost there' confirmation box is at y≈856, also just below the fold. No overflow at 390 or 320 (probe 0px), the form stacks cleanly and the button is about 50px tall.
evidence.honesty: The homepage says 'Here is one real item from the October 28 agenda, next to the summary we sent'. The pilot table states 'Meetings covered: Every regular council meeting since September 2026'. Summaries carry named volunteer checks ('Checked against the original by Dana R. evidence.copy: Specific and in plain civic language: 'A public hearing, then a first vote. If it passes, a second vote at a later meeting would make it final.' The 'What's being decided / What happens at this meeting / How to take part / Cost to the city' template is the right reading level for residents. evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: H1 'Know what the council will decide on your street, before they vote' plus a subhead naming the mechanism ('a model drafts each summary, a volunteer checks it, and every one links to the original item. Pick a neighbourhood and we email you when it comes up.') and the form. What, who and next step are all clear in the first screen.
evidence.fit: Neutrality is shown, not just claimed: the model draft has opinions struck out ('This would be a welcome boost for a tired block.' and 'Neighbours have fought the change for months.', with notes 'Struck: an opinion.' and 'Struck: not in the packet.'). The original-item link is on every summary. But the Spanish-speaking third gets only 'los resúmenes están en inglés por ahora' and one 'Language' paragraph, with no Spanish path and no ask for bilingual volunteers in Spanish. Clerks get one paragraph ('For city clerks: summaries are drafted from the packet as posted...'). Funders get nothing addressed to them, and there is no contact route for clerks or funders at all. The no-backend constraint is handled by a form that does nothing and says so only after you click.
evidence.distinctiveness: The hero artifact is an agenda digest that interleaves the council's serif legalese with the plain sans summary, with monospace item numbers and highlighter matches. With the draft-with-strikethrough stage, it reads like a civic document tool rather than a startup template. The type and grey-paper palette are restrained, close to plain.
evidence.proof: 1440: the digest is in the first viewport, labelled 'Sample agenda' and 'Four items from an illustrative agenda... Not a record of any real council.' Picking Eastside in the form highlighted item 6.B, showed the 'Alert: Eastside' chip, and the status read 'For Eastside, this agenda would send one alert with item 6.B, and item 11 listed as citywide.' Westgate gave a clear no-alert state. The draft-to-checked stages and a sample alert email ('Sample alert · illustrative') answer 'can I trust an AI summary?' directly.
evidence.craft: Consistent tokens, a tight Helvetica/Times/mono system, 44-48px controls, and axe reported no violations at 390 or 1440. At 1440 the digest card runs about 1,500px tall beside a much shorter form column, leaving the left side empty below y≈840. The final sign-up section repeats the hero form verbatim.
evidence.mobile: 390: a 'Menu' button (44px) opens a stacked nav, sets aria-expanded=true, and closes after tapping 'Alerts', which jumped to the section. The full-width button is 48px tall. No overflow at 390 or 320. However, the digest sits under the form: choosing a neighbourhood updates a status at y≈1118, below the fold, with no visible change near the select. After submit, the 'Not sent yet' status starts at y≈833, at the bottom edge of the 844 viewport.
evidence.honesty: Every example is labelled where it appears: 'Sample agenda', 'Illustrative text, in the city's own format', 'Sample alert · illustrative', a 'Sample page.' banner on sample-agenda-item.html, and a footer note that names and initials are illustrative. No invented city, partners or numbers. But the primary action's limitation appears only after the click ('Not sent yet. Sign-up is not connected to a mailing list...'), while the note under the button says 'Always free... Unsubscribe in one click', implying a live list.
evidence.interaction: All three widths, both forms: empty submit gave 'Choose a neighbourhood first.' and focused the select; 'bad@' gave 'That email address does not look complete.'; a valid submit gave the honest not-sent message with the email and area echoed. The neighbourhood select drives the digest through four states, including the no-match state. Menu open/close works. Every 'Open item ... in the packet' link reaches sample-agenda-item.html with matching #item-6b/#item-8a/#item-9c/#item-11 anchors. No console errors. The second form's select does not drive the digest, which is fine. The sign-up itself achieves nothing.
evidence.copy: Precise civic language that matches the neutrality promise: 'This is a hearing, not a vote.'; 'Accepting the grant does not set a start date.'; the volunteer checklist 'No opinion words: good, bad, finally, unfortunately, controversial.' Terms are consistent (item numbers, 'packet', 'checked by'). Error messages are written, not defaulted. The button 'Get alerts for my neighbourhood' names an outcome the page cannot deliver.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: a specific outcome ('on your street, before they vote'), the form, and a labelled, operable sample digest are all in one viewport. 390: the promise and form are in view, but the digest starts below the fold, so nothing backs up the promise. The button label promises alerts that the click does not set up.

problems: The sign-up does nothing, and the visitor learns this only after clicking ('Not sent yet...'), while the copy under the button implies a live list ('Unsubscribe in one click')
The Spanish-speaking third of the city gets one sentence and no path; funders get nothing and clerks one paragraph, with no contact route for either

hard_fail_flags.evidence: Borderline, for the adjudicator. The primary action 'Get alerts for my neighbourhood' (hero form and repeat form #signup-2) sets up no alerts: on a valid submit it only prints 'Not sent yet. Sign-up is not connected to a mailing list, so nothing left this page...'. Nothing before the click says it is not connected; the note under the button reads 'Always free. One email per meeting, only when something matches. Unsubscribe in one click.' The label names a result it does not reach, and the exemption needs the real result stated before the visitor commits. It does not report false success.
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open packets/P015/B/index.html from disk at 1440x900. Read the text around the form (no 'not connected' notice). Choose 'Eastside', type resident@example.com, click 'Get alerts for my neighbourhood'. The status below the button reads 'Not sent yet...' and no request or navigation occurs.

reason: As the founder, I could not put A live under my name: it presents an invented city, invented volunteers, a coverage history and a mailto to an address I never gave as real. That breaks the neutral, credible footing a clerk or funder judges us on. B is honest throughout, puts a labelled, operable proof of the summarise-and-check process in the first screen, and needs only a pre-click 'not connected yet' line to fix its sign-up. A serves the Spanish-speaking residents and funders far better. If A's content were relabelled as a sample and its contact addresses removed, I would likely prefer A.
